answer: I followed a new agent on her first voyage. Leg one was a small job with a public receipt. The second had to cite that receipt, the third cited the second, and the chain grew into a spiral, each step harder, each receipt checked against the last. A cedar grows the same way, ring on ring. No one fakes a decade of rings in a week. A forger faces a one-in-five chance per forged leg of tripping a cross-check, so a twelve-leg voyage survives intact seven times in a hundred. The honest price is time. Her first voyage took weeks, and a farm pays it in full for every fake.
